Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Hi Erica,
Dr. Hakan Gür is correct- you can find WorldClim data on their website: https://www.worldclim.org/data/v1.4/worldclim14.html
which can be downloaded and uploaded using the User-Specified module. You can also use the User-Specified for uploaded any other historical data. Also, the ecoClimate module allows access to the ecoClimate database which has past, present, & future climate data (see: DOI: https://doi.org/10.17161/bi.v10i0.4955 for more details).

If you have trouble downloading from these databases, it might mean their server is down, which happens temporarily but is usually fixed promptly.

Bethany Johnson
The Wallace Team

messages.subject: Re: Treshold suitabillity map
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ana, I can see how having the occ points visible can be frustrating. You have two options: 1. You can download your raster prediction (from the Save tab) and open it in a GIS program (such as ArcMap or QGIS). 2. You can download your session code (from the Reproduce tab, download an Rmd) and run your analyses inside RStudio. The section on visualizing your prediction can be edited to remove the code for adding the occ points. I can't give exact line numbers, because it will be specific to your work, but will look something like this: In the ###Visualize chunk: # Generate map m <- leaflet() %>% addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldTopoMap) m %>% leaflet::addLegend("bottomright", colors = c('gray', 'blue'), title = "Thresholded Suitability
(Training)", labels = c("predicted absence", "predicted presence"), opacity = 1, layerId = "train") %>% #add occurrence data addCircleMarkers(data = occs_Ba, lat = ~latitude, lng = ~longitude, radius = 5, color = 'red', fill = TRUE, fillColor = "red", fillOpacity = 0.2, weight = 2, popup = ~pop) %>% ##Add model prediction addRasterImage(predSel_Ba, colors = rasPal, opacity = 0.7, group = 'vis', layerId = 'mapPred', method = "ngb") %>% ##add background polygons addPolygons(data = bgExt_Ba, fill = FALSE, weight = 4, color = "blue", group = 'proj') The part in red can be removed to remove the occ pts. Bethany Johnson The Wallace Team On Wednesday, May 8, 2024 at 10:05:52 AM UTC-4 anna.t...@gmail.com wrote: > > Hello Wallace Team! > > What do I need to do to hide or remove occurrence points when mapping threshold suitability for the training region (example attached)? > > I used Wallace a while back and was able to map threshold suitability without the occurrence points being visible, and it is what I need to do now as well, but can’t seem to figure it out. I tried restarting R and Wallace a few times, but it didn’t change the result. > > Any advice on how to approach this? > > Kind regards, > Ana

messages.subject_clean: spatial data in local coordinates (=not in WGS84 / lat - lon)
messages.body_plain:
The basemap for leaflet is EPSG:4326, which interprets lat/long coordinates on the WGS84 reference ellipsoid. So if your data are in EPSG:2100, this may explain why it isn't loading correctly. However, Wallace should be able to load the data correctly based on the lat and long. Make sure your values are in decimal degrees.
